newsitem.title: USA: Chubb to accelerate share buybacks in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Chubb to accelerate share buybacks in 1997.

text.p: Chubb Corp plans to become more aggressive this year in buying back its shares, paying for them with proceeds from the planned sale of its life insurance business, analysts said after a conference call with the company on Thursday.
Chubb Chief Executive Dean O'Hare "volunteered that, yes indeed, he will be using the proceeds to accelerate a Chubb stock repurchase program," Salomon Brothers analyst Michael Smith said.
O'Hare, who spoke after the stock market close, did not specify how much the company expected to spend on a buyback program, the analysts said.
O'Hare told analysts that Chubb bought back 500,000 shares in the fourth quarter of 1996 and a total of 1.7 million during the year, Peter Wade of Lehman Brothers said.
Chubb said it would not spend more than the proceeds of the sale on repurchasing stock, Wade said.
The life insurance business has a current book value of about $850 million. Wade said he thought the business would sell for less than book value.
O'Hare also told analysts he expected the company to achieve return on equity of 15 percent after its restructuring. It will later raise its target to 16 to 17 percent, he said.

He also told analysts he expected premium growth of 16 percent in the property-casualty business this year. Such an increase would in part reflect the termination of a quota share agreement with Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc, Wade said.
O'Hare said domestic premium growth was expected to reach about 7.5 percent, and international growth to range from eight to 20 percent, excluding Canada, Wade said.
O'Hare told analysts that Chubb's fourth-quarter earnings fell short of forecasts because of higher-than-expected catastrophe losses.
That followed a disappointing third-quarter earnings performance, which was hindered by a sharp increase in catastrophe losses as well.
With the unwinding of Chubb's quota share reinsurance agreement with Royal & Sun, Chubb may now have more risk exposure in certain regions, Salomon's Smith said.
And the increased exposure to catastrophes is likely to hurt Chubb's price/earnings multiples and force analysts to lower their earnings forecasts, Smith said.
The fourth-quarter earnings disappointment, Smith said, is likely to outweigh the news about the share buyback.
"What's new is that this company can't seem to hit earnings estimates anymore," he said.
